title: Token-Aware Routing
summary: Route work according to estimated context and output demand while preserving capability, evidence quality, and a hard task-level token budget.
overview: Token-aware routing uses input size, expected output length, context-window limits, and remaining budget to choose an execution path. The destination may be a smaller model, a larger-context model, a retrieval step, a condensation stage, or an asynchronous job. Token count is a capacity signal, not a reliable measure of task difficulty.

Estimate the complete request: system instructions, tool schemas, retrieved evidence, conversation state, and reserved output all consume capacity. A short request can require difficult reasoning, while a long document may need simple extraction. Apply capability and policy constraints before optimizing token cost.

production.poc: A prototype can compare token estimates with actual usage across a representative request set. Include multilingual text, tables, and tool-heavy prompts.
production.production: Production reserves output and tool-loop capacity, rejects impossible requests early, and reconciles estimated versus billed usage. Use model-specific tokenization where available rather than a universal characters-per-token rule.
production.scale: At scale, tenant budgets and provider quotas shape routing decisions. Track truncation, fallback frequency, and downstream correction cost so apparently cheap routes do not increase total cost per successful task.

components.name: Prompt estimator
components.role: Counts or estimates all input segments and reserves expected output capacity.

components.name: Capability filter
components.role: Removes models and paths that cannot meet task, policy, or residency requirements.

components.name: Budget allocator
components.role: Assigns per-step token ceilings from the remaining task allowance.

components.name: Routing policy
components.role: Selects extraction, retrieval, condensation, or model execution using validated thresholds.

components.name: Usage reconciler
components.role: Records actual consumption and updates estimates without changing completed accounting.

flow.title: Measure request
flow.description: Estimate instructions, schemas, history, evidence, and expected output using the candidate model's tokenizer.

flow.title: Check feasibility
flow.description: Verify context fit and reserve capacity for mandatory validation or additional tool observations.

flow.title: Filter capability
flow.description: Exclude paths that lack required language, reasoning, structure, or data-handling support.

flow.title: Select strategy
flow.description: Choose direct execution, smaller context retrieval, condensation, or a suitable model.

flow.title: Enforce limits
flow.description: Apply output ceilings and stop optional iterations before exhausting the parent budget.

flow.title: Reconcile outcome
flow.description: Record actual tokens, quality, and fallback cost to evaluate routing economics.

diagrams.caption: Token demand determines feasible strategies only after required capabilities and policy are respected.

useCase.title: Processing broker submission packages
useCase.situation: A specialty insurer receives submissions ranging from short forms to lengthy engineering reports with scanned appendices.
useCase.problem: Routing by file size alone sends difficult short submissions to weak models and wastes large-context calls on irrelevant attachments.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must extract specified underwriting facts with source references under a per-submission processing budget.
useCase.architecture: A tokenizer-aware estimator combines document structure with capability requirements and routes relevant sections to extraction or deeper review.
runtime: The ingestion service identifies attachments and estimates prompt demand; retrieval selects evidence for each required field.
Simple tables use a compact extraction path, while ambiguous exclusions use a stronger eligible model with reserved verification capacity.
useCase.failure: If estimates understate a scanned report's token demand, the system partitions evidence by semantic section rather than silently truncating required material.
useCase.impact: Measure tokens per accepted field, context overflow, unsupported extraction, and total fallback cost. A lower model bill is useful only if review quality remains acceptable.

tradeoffs.benefit: Routine extraction can consume less inference capacity.
tradeoffs.cost: Capability mismatch can increase corrections and retries.

tradeoffs.benefit: More requests fit available context windows.
tradeoffs.cost: Evidence details may be lost and require retrieval again.

tradeoffs.benefit: Cost exposure becomes predictable per task.
tradeoffs.cost: Difficult cases may need escalation before full completion.

failures.detection: Actual input usage exceeds the estimate before evidence is included.
failures.recovery: Include all prompt segments and adjust reservations.

failures.detection: Usage ledger shows high total cost despite low initial spend.
failures.recovery: Change routing thresholds using end-to-end outcomes.

mistakes.mistake: Equating short prompts with easy tasks
mistakes.fix: Evaluate task capability independently from length.

mistakes.mistake: Truncating evidence to force context fit
mistakes.fix: Retrieve or partition while preserving required coverage.
Budget input, output, and follow-up observations together.

whenToUse: Requests vary substantially in context and output size.
Several capable execution paths have different token economics.
Task-level spend and context limits must be enforced.
whenNotToUse: One model and fixed-size prompts already meet constraints.
Quality cannot be measured across candidate routes.
Routing overhead exceeds plausible token savings.
